title: Fourth Word Explaining The Comparison And Its Rational Measure

questions.question: In the comparison, who does the ruler stand for?
questions.answer: The ruler stands for Allah, the Sustainer and Creator.

questions.question: What do the two traveling servants represent?
questions.answer: One represents people who are careful and sincere in prayer, and the other represents people who are careless and leave prayer.

questions.question: What do the twenty-four gold coins symbolize?
questions.answer: They symbolize the twenty-four hours of a day in a person’s life.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the royal estate represent?
questions.answer: It represents Paradise.

questions.question: What does the station in the comparison stand for?
questions.answer: It stands for the grave.

questions.question: How is the journey explained in the passage?
questions.answer: It is the human journey from this life to the grave, then to resurrection and the hereafter.

questions.question: According to the passage, why do people move through that journey at different levels?
questions.answer: Their progress differs based on what they do and how strong their taqwa is.

questions.question: What is the ticket meant to represent?
questions.answer: It represents the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: About how much time each day does the passage say is needed for the five daily prayers and ablution?
questions.answer: About one hour.

questions.question: Why is it described as a serious loss to spend almost the whole day on worldly life and not give one hour to prayer?
questions.answer: Because worldly life is short, but the hereafter is lasting, so neglecting prayer means wasting what helps a person prepare for what matters most.

questions.question: What example is given to show how unreasonable it is to neglect prayer?
questions.answer: The passage compares it to someone risking a huge amount for a very unlikely prize but refusing to invest a small amount in something with a far greater and more certain return.

questions.question: According to the passage, what benefits does prayer bring to the inner life of a person?
questions.answer: It brings comfort to the soul, heart, and mind.

questions.question: How does the passage describe prayer in relation to the body?
questions.answer: It says prayer is not a heavy burden for the body.

questions.question: With the right intention, what can happen to a person’s other daily actions?
questions.answer: They can also count as acts of worship.

questions.question: How can a person, through prayer and right intention, turn temporary life into something lasting in one sense?
questions.answer: By using daily life for the sake of the hereafter, a person can send the reward of that life forward and give it lasting value.

questions.question: What is the main religious practice being urged in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage urges people to perform the five daily prayers.

questions.question: Who is directly being addressed at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: People who do not pray and the speaker’s own self that resists prayer are being addressed.

questions.question: What does the devout servant show about a person’s attitude toward salah?
questions.answer: He shows eagerness, seriousness, and care in fulfilling prayer.

questions.question: What does the neglectful servant show?
questions.answer: He shows heedlessness and failure to give prayer its proper place.

questions.question: Why do the twenty-four coins fit well as a symbol in the comparison?
questions.answer: Because they match the twenty-four hours Allah gives a person each day.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relationship between this world and the hereafter?
questions.answer: It teaches that this world is a passage and preparation, while the hereafter is the lasting destination.

questions.question: What does the mention of the grave remind the reader of?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader that death is certain and that every person is moving toward meeting what comes after this life.

questions.question: What determines how quickly or well people cross the long journey described in the passage?
questions.answer: Their deeds and the strength of their awareness and fear of Allah affect it.

questions.question: Why does the passage call prayer a “ticket”?
questions.answer: Because prayer is presented as something that helps a person reach the eternal destination safely and successfully.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the amount of effort needed for prayer compared with its reward?
questions.answer: It suggests the effort is small, but the reward is enormous.

questions.question: What is wrong with spending nearly all one’s time only on worldly concerns, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It means a person ignores the eternal future for the sake of a short and passing life.

questions.question: How does the lottery example strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that people would normally seek the better and more certain gain, so ignoring prayer is clearly irrational.

questions.question: Which human faculties are said to find relief in prayer?
questions.answer: The soul, heart, and mind.

questions.question: What important condition is mentioned for everyday actions to become worship?
questions.answer: A sincere and proper intention is required.

questions.question: What overall message does the final sentence of the passage give about human life?
questions.answer: It teaches that prayer and right intention can make a short worldly life fruitful for eternity.

questions.question: In that same symbolism, what does the grave correspond to?
questions.answer: It corresponds to the stopping place on the journey.

questions.question: What daily resource has Allah given every person, according to the image of the gold pieces?
questions.answer: He has given each person the hours of the day.

questions.question: What is the difference between the two servants in spiritual terms?
questions.answer: One is obedient and devoted in worship, while the other is careless and neglectful.

questions.question: Why is the grave described as a station rather than the final destination?
questions.answer: Because the passage teaches that life continues beyond death into resurrection and the hereafter.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that some cross very great distances quickly?
questions.answer: It suggests that righteousness and taqwa help a person advance with great speed and ease toward the next life.

questions.question: What simple time commitment does the passage say prayer requires each day?
questions.answer: It says the five prayers with purification take about one hour in total.

questions.question: Why is neglecting that one hour described as a person wronging himself?
questions.answer: Because he deprives himself of something that would benefit him greatly in the hereafter.

questions.question: What kind of person is criticized through the financial comparison in the passage?
questions.answer: A person who claims to be sensible but makes choices that ignore obvious eternal benefit.

questions.question: What contrast is being made between a risky gamble and prayer?
questions.answer: The gamble has weak odds and uncertain gain, while prayer leads toward a far surer and greater reward.

questions.question: Besides reward in the hereafter, what immediate effect does prayer have on a person’s inner state?
questions.answer: It gives peace and ease to the inner self.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the physical side of prayer?
questions.answer: It says the body is not overburdened by it.

questions.question: How can ordinary actions become spiritually valuable?
questions.answer: If they are done with the right intention by a person who performs prayer, they can take on the value of worship.

questions.question: What is one major lesson a Muslim student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: A small, regular act of obedience like salah brings deep inner benefit and prepares a person for eternal success.

questions.question: What is being explained through the story of the ruler and the two servants in this passage?
questions.answer: The story explains the meaning and importance of the daily prayers.

questions.question: How is the ruler described in terms of belief?
questions.answer: He represents the Lord who created and sustains all people.

questions.question: What moral difference separates the two servants?
questions.answer: One is serious about worship, while the other is spiritually careless.

questions.question: Why do the gold coins represent time instead of money in the explanation?
questions.answer: Because the point is about how a person spends each day of life, not mainly about wealth.

questions.question: What destination is placed before the reader as the true homeland?
questions.answer: The true homeland is Paradise.

questions.question: What role does the grave play in the passage’s view of life?
questions.answer: It is a stage every person must pass through on the way to the next world.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the effect of taqwa on a person’s future?
questions.answer: It helps a person move forward more successfully on the journey to the hereafter.

questions.question: Why is the prayer compared to something that allows travel?
questions.answer: Because it helps carry a person toward eternal success, like travel access helps someone reach a destination.

questions.question: What point is made by saying the prayers take only about one hour?
questions.answer: The point is that prayer asks for little time compared with the huge value it gives.

questions.question: According to the passage, what mistake does a person make by using nearly the whole day only for dunya?
questions.answer: He treats temporary life as if it matters more than eternal life.

questions.question: What does the example of unequal chances of gain teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that refusing a highly beneficial and reliable investment is foolish.

questions.question: How does prayer affect a person emotionally and mentally?
questions.answer: It brings relief and calm to the inner being and the mind.

questions.question: What does the passage say about prayer as a physical task?
questions.answer: It presents prayer as manageable and not harsh on the body.

questions.question: What transforms everyday actions into worship according to the passage?
questions.answer: A sound intention joined with faithful prayer transforms them.

questions.question: How does the passage present the value of human life?
questions.answer: It presents life as a capital that should be invested for the hereafter rather than wasted on what quickly passes.

questions.question: Who is represented by the servant who prays eagerly?
questions.answer: He represents believers who perform their prayers with devotion.

questions.question: Who is represented by the servant who neglects his duty?
questions.answer: He represents those who are careless about prayer.

questions.question: What part of human life is symbolized by the twenty-four coins?
questions.answer: They symbolize the full day a person receives.

questions.question: What does the passage identify as the final blessed destination?
questions.answer: It identifies Paradise as the blessed destination.

questions.question: According to the passage, what lies between worldly life and the hereafter?
questions.answer: The grave lies between them as a stage on the way.

questions.question: How does the passage describe differences among people in making that journey?
questions.answer: Some advance much more quickly than others because of their deeds and taqwa.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the ticket in the comparison?
questions.answer: It means the prescribed prayers that prepare and carry a person toward the next life.

questions.question: How much time does the passage say this “ticket” requires each day?
questions.answer: It requires about one hour for prayer and ablution.

questions.question: Why is a person’s behavior called irrational if he ignores that one hour?
questions.answer: Because he sacrifices lasting benefit for short-term distractions.

questions.question: How does the passage use numbers and probability to persuade the reader?
questions.answer: It shows that prayer offers far greater and surer gain than the kinds of risks people often accept in worldly matters.

questions.question: What three parts of a person are said to gain comfort from prayer?
questions.answer: The spirit, the heart, and the mind.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the burden of prayer on the body?
questions.answer: It says prayer is not difficult for the body.

questions.question: What can happen to a praying person’s normal activities if his intention is right?
questions.answer: They can be counted as worship.

questions.question: What is the broader life lesson at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: A believer can use daily life in a way that gives it enduring value instead of letting it pass away empty.

questions.question: What central idea is taught through the explanation of the comparison?
questions.answer: The central idea is that the daily prayers are essential, reasonable, and deeply beneficial for a Muslim’s life and afterlife.

questions.question: In the explained comparison, whom does the ruler point to?
questions.answer: He points to Allah, the Lord of all.

questions.question: What do the two servants reveal about two kinds of people?
questions.answer: They reveal the difference between those who commit to prayer and those who neglect it.

questions.question: Why is each day compared to a set amount of treasure?
questions.answer: Because every day gives a person limited but valuable time that must be used wisely.

questions.question: What does the royal property represent in spiritual terms?
questions.answer: It represents the eternal reward of Paradise.

questions.question: What truth is emphasized by calling the grave a station?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that death is not the end but part of the journey to what comes after.

questions.question: On what two things does the speed of that journey depend, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It depends on a person’s deeds and on the strength of his fear and awareness of Allah.

questions.question: Why is salah compared to a ticket instead of just any good deed?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as a necessary means of reaching the destination safely and successfully.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the balance between time spent on dunya and time spent on salah?
questions.answer: It suggests that giving nearly all time to dunya and neglecting salah is a badly distorted balance.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says such a person harms himself?
questions.answer: It means he deprives himself of eternal benefit and acts against his own true good.

questions.question: What reasoning is used in the example about investing wealth?
questions.answer: It uses the logic that any sensible person should choose the far more secure and lasting gain.

questions.question: What inward benefits of prayer are named in the passage?
questions.answer: Prayer gives comfort and ease to a person’s inner life, especially the soul, heart, and mind.

questions.question: What practical benefit does the passage mention for the rest of a praying person’s day?
questions.answer: The rest of his actions can also become worship if his intention is sincere.

questions.question: How does this passage connect intention with ordinary life?
questions.answer: It teaches that intention can lift normal daily actions into spiritually meaningful deeds.

questions.question: If you had to state the message of the whole passage in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: Use your daily time for prayer and sincere obedience so your short worldly life becomes an investment for eternal success.
